The Child Who Says "I'm bored, are we there yet?"

Stuck in traffic, waiting in a clinic lobby, or at a restaurant, a child squirms and repeats "I'm bored." They stamp their feet and pout.

Showing them a video quiets them for a moment, but it doesn't build the child's own ability to handle boredom. The real tool for turning boredom into fun is imagination.

Curious about the pretend play story? Let's look at the lesson of the pretend play story through the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the pretend play story too. When You're Bored, Play Pretend!"—creativity stories, beating boredom, growing imagination, and more.

content.alt: 30. When You're Bored, Play Pretend! - Boredom Becomes the Raw Material of Creativity
content.text:
Boredom Becomes the Raw Material of Creativity

Boredom isn't a bad thing. In fact, it can be the starting point of creativity, where a child invents their own play.

A child who often experiences turning dull moments into imagination finds joy instead of frustration in the face of boredom. This ability becomes the root of the creativity that lets them see problems from new angles, even as they grow up.

content.alt: 30. When You're Bored, Play Pretend! - Hori and Mom's Pretend Play
content.text:
Hori and Mom's Pretend Play

In the story When You're Bored, Play Pretend!, Hori is bored stuck in traffic. That's when Mom suggests, "Imagine your seat is a great big boat!"

When Hori closes his eyes, his car seat becomes a boat rocking on the waves. The red traffic light is a magic star, and the puffy clouds are fluffy sheep! As Hori and Mom take turns imagining, the once-boring view out the window becomes full of wonders.

content.alt: 30. When You're Bored, Play Pretend! - 3 Pretend Games You Learn from Tangobook
content.text:
3 Pretend Games You Learn from Tangobook

The heart of this story is three things that are easy for a child to try. One, imagine the object in front of you as something else! Two, turn the clouds outside into animals! Three, take turns with Mom continuing the story!

Tangobook's stories repeat these games like a refrain, helping a child naturally recall them in a boring moment. Just like Hori, who turned boredom into fun, a child learns how to invent their own play.

content.alt: 30. When You're Bored, Play Pretend! - Take-Turns Pretend Play to Do Together at Home
content.text:
Take-Turns Pretend Play to Do Together at Home

After reading, when a boring moment comes, ask, "What does that cloud look like?" or "What could this chair become?" When the parent goes once and the child goes once, taking turns, it becomes a game.

Don't ask for a right answer here. The sillier the imagination, the better. When you joyfully welcome free imagination, a child builds the power to turn boredom into fun all on their own.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How do I play with my child when they're bored?

A. Even without toys, you can create a whole joyful world through pretend play. When you're bored, play pretend and make up a story together—creativity grows by leaps and bounds.

Q. How does a pretend play story help my child?

A. Like the hero in the story, a child grows the imagination to turn ordinary moments into special adventures. A pretend play story builds the power to create fun on their own.

Q. How can I best join in on pretend play?

A. Rather than setting a right answer for your child's silly imaginings, cheer them on with excitement. When parents join in joyfully, a child's imagination unfolds even wider and freer.
